runbooks.diagnosis: Let's Encrypt rate limits hit — usually after repeated re-creation of the traefik container with a lost acme.json or a wildcard/san burst. The LE staging/duplicate limit is 5 failures per hour, 50 certs per week per domain.
remediation: Stop recreating the traefik container; preserve the acme.json volume across restarts
Verify the requested domains (duplicate certificate limit is 5/week)
Wait out the rate-limit window (1h for validations, 7d for certificates)
Switch to the LE staging endpoint while debugging issuance

runbooks.diagnosis: Traefik did not pick up the dynamic config or the target container has no matching router labels/network attachment. Most common in this stack: service is on a different compose network than traefik, or the router rule host mismatches the requested domain.
remediation: Confirm the service shares the traefik network (opensme-net)
Compare the router rule host with the actual request Host header
Check traefik logs for 'router ... error' lines naming the service
Restart traefik only after config verification

runbooks.diagnosis: acme.json must be 0600; Docker volume copies can reset permissions and traefik refuses to start with a world-readable acme file.
remediation: chmod 600 the acme.json inside the traefik-data volume
